nodes.title: Rational and complex representations
nodes.statement: For a polarized complex abelian variety A=V/Λ of dimension g, a Z-basis of Λ and a complex basis of V give injective ring representations ρ:End(A)→Mat(2g,Z) and κ:End(A)→Mat(g,C). For a period matrix P their convention is κ(v)P=Pρ(v). In normalized principally polarized coordinates with P=(I,τ), block signs are chosen so that ρ=[[a,−b],[−c,d]] and κ=a−τc. Extend both representations Q-linearly to End⁰(A). Changing either basis conjugates the corresponding representation.
proofSteps: Apply the existing complex-lattice functor to each native homomorphism.
Choose bases and write the induced lattice map and complex-linear tangent map; the exponential comparison gives κP=Pρ.
Injectivity follows because Λ spans V over R; conjugation follows from ordinary basis change.

This is a norm on the finite-dimensional real scalar extension of End⁰(A). It is not the regular algebra trace and does not require † to preserve the integral order.
proofSteps: Use A6 positivity for the real positive quadratic form.
Take its nonnegative square root; derive the norm axioms by the associated inner product.

nodes.title: Rosati discriminant
nodes.statement: For an order O=End_k(A) or End_k̄(A), choose a Z-basis e₁,…,e_r of its finite free underlying group and define Dλ(O)=det(Tr_A(e_i e_j†))>0. For rank zero set the empty determinant equal to 1. It is independent of the basis. Under a principal polarization the pairing is integral, hence Dλ(O) is a positive integer. For a nonprincipal λ the same positive rational determinant is allowed; do not assume integral adjoints. For End_k use a k-defined polarization so the rational involution preserves End⁰_k; the geometric order uses a geometric polarization.
proofSteps: Use the imported finite free End lattice.
A basis change with determinant±1 preserves the Gram determinant.
Positivity and principal integrality follow from A6; the covolume identity is imported from GN.0.

nodes.title: Degree polynomial in coordinates
nodes.statement: Let A,B be complex abelian varieties of the same dimension g, and use positively oriented Z-bases of their period lattices. For f in Hom(A,B), deg(f)=det ρ(f), where degree is the finite-kernel degree for an isogeny and zero otherwise. Consequently deg(∑ t_i f_i)=det(∑ t_i ρ(f_i)) is a homogeneous polynomial of total degree 2g in the rational variables t_i, or the zero polynomial. The same assertion holds for number-field varieties after a complex embedding. For g=0 the empty determinant and polynomial are 1.
proofSteps: For an isogeny f:V/Λ→W/Λ′, its kernel has order [Λ′:fΛ]=|det ρ(f)|. Complex-linear maps preserve real orientation, so the determinant is nonnegative with the stated oriented bases. Finite isogenies in characteristic zero are étale, so kernel order equals degree.
A nonisogeny between equal-dimensional abelian varieties has rank-deficient real representation and determinant zero.

The determinant of a 2g by 2g matrix of linear forms is homogeneous of degree 2g. Extend to rational Hom by clearing denominators. Degree and lattice realization commute with the chosen characteristic-zero base change.
acceptance: For [n] obtain n^(2g), including negative n.
For Hom(E²,E²), a diagonal map (1,0) has degree zero; a shear has degree one.
For g=0 keep degree 1; the positive-dimensional zero-map test must not be applied.

proofSteps: For an isogeny the determinant of the real representation is its positive degree.
Apply AM–GM to the 2g squared singular values and take a square root.
The nonisogeny case has degree 0; clear denominators for rational endomorphisms.

nodes.title: Coordinate trace formula
nodes.statement: In normalized principally polarized coordinates write τ=x+iy in Siegel space and let ε be the standard alternating matrix in the chosen symplectic lattice basis. Then qλ(v)=tr(ρ(v)ερ(v)ᵀε⁻¹)=2 Re tr(κ(v)y overline(κ(v))ᵀy⁻¹). The bilinear Gram entry is 2 Re tr(κ(v)y overline(κ(w))ᵀy⁻¹). In orthonormal real coordinates this becomes tr(MMᵀ).
proofSteps: Express Rosati as the adjoint for the Riemann form.
Compute the rational adjoint matrix and pass to the Hermitian complex matrix.
Realify the complex trace; check v=w=1 and v=i on the square CM curve.

nodes.title: Regular-trace order discriminant
nodes.statement: Let B be a finite-dimensional semisimple Q-algebra of Q-dimension m, and O⊂B a unital full Z-lattice subring. Puttr_B(x)=Tr_Q(L_x:B→B), the regular trace, anddisc(O)=det(tr_B(e_i e_j)) for a Z-basis. Retain the sign and use|disc(O)| in inequalities. Division algebras and isotypic matrix algebras are both included. This refines the existing algebra/lattice carriers and creates no second CSA, order or lattice type.
proofSteps: Use the existing full lattice and left multiplication linear map.
The determinant changes by the square of an integral basis-change determinant.

For nondegeneracy, use Artin–Wedderburn block matrices over finite-dimensional division Q-algebras. Given a nonzero entry x_ij in one block, choose the single-entry matrix y_ji=x_ij⁻¹ in that block and zero elsewhere. Then tr_B(xy)=n·dim_Q(D)≠0 for that n×n block. This proves the regular-trace pairing nondegenerate without importing a reduced-trace theorem.

nodes.title: Order class index
nodes.statement: Let D be a finite-dimensional division Q-algebra and O⊂D a unital full Z-lattice subring. For e≥1 consider finitely generated left O-modules M whose underlying abelian group is Z-torsion-free and whose rationalization Q⊗_Z M is a left D-vector space of dimension e. Let b(M) be the least additive index [M:F] among free left O-submodules F≅O^e of full Z-rank. Such F exist by clearing denominators in a D-basis. Define i_e(O)=sup_M b(M) in N∪{∞}; also i_0(O)=1. Finiteness is the class-index theorem, not a defining assumption.
proofSteps: RepresentM as a lattice in D^e after a rational basis choice.
Clear common denominators to embedO^e and take the least positive finite index.
Take the supremum in the extended naturals so that the definition does not presuppose Jordan–Zassenhaus finiteness.

Transport right modules to left modules over the opposite algebra. For x∈D, the subalgebra Q[x] is a field; its left and right actions on D have equal dimension over Q[x], so L_x and R_x have equal rational trace. Cyclicity gives tr_D(yx)=tr_D(xy), hence the opposite order has the same regular-trace discriminant.

nodes.title: Division-algebra norm body
nodes.statement: Let D be a finite-dimensional division Q-algebra of Q-dimension m≥1. Put N_D(x)=det_Q(L_x), extended to D_R. In any full rational lattice basis Λ put p(D)=sqrt(|disc(Λ)|) times the supremum of the coordinate volumes of bounded convex bodies C with nonempty interior, C=−C, and C⊂{x:|N_D(x)|<1}. Symmetry is about zero. Strict interior may be replaced by limiting compact bodies. The product is independent of Λ and the chosen basis; it is a positive finite real number, with upper bound supplied by Minkowski applied to any full order lattice.
proofSteps: Transform the regular-trace determinant and Lebesgue coordinate volume under the same basis change; their factors cancel.
Use a sufficiently small Euclidean ball for positivity.

For a full order lattice, every nonzero integral vector has nonzero integral regular norm. Minkowski therefore bounds the volume of any eligible symmetric convex body; this proves finiteness of the supremum.

Filter a rank-e lattice by a rational D-line; lift a free sublattice of the quotient and combine it with a rank-one sublattice to provei_e≤i_1 i_(e−1).

nodes.title: Isotypic trace comparison
nodes.statement: Let A be isotypic of dimension g≥1 and O=End_k(A) of Q-rank m, where the k-isotypic decomposition and its rational endomorphism algebra use the same field. For every k-defined polarization λ, (2g)^m |disc(O)|=m^m Dλ(O), with disc computed using regular trace on End⁰_k(A). The same formula holds geometrically with geometric isotypy and geometric End. No such single proportionality is asserted for arbitrary products of nonisogenous factors.
proofSteps: Compare both traces after writingEnd⁰ as one matrix algebra over a division algebra; the ratio is m/(2g).
The Rosati involution is an involutive rational linear map, so its determinant is±1 even if it fails to preserveO.
Take determinants of the two bilinear forms and absolute values.

nodes.title: Hom cross-discriminant
nodes.statement: Let A,B/k be k-simple k-isogenous abelian varieties of dimension g. Put M=Hom_k(B,A), M′=Hom_k(A,B), and D=End⁰_k(A), of Q-dimension m. The pairing M×M′→Q is(u,v)↦tr_D(u∘v). Define c(M,M′)=det(pairing in Z-bases)², a positive rational number independent of bases. It is the square of the determinant, not its absolute value.
proofSteps: The rational Hom spaces are one-dimensional over the appropriate division algebra, so the trace pairing is perfect.
Choose integral bases and square its determinant.
Independent unimodular changes on either side change only its sign before squaring.
